cases.note: Contested is only whether the status list has a-v when enqueue builds it from the full form (Q-OF-11, OF-V5). windmill-lite's reference configuration is the successful lite deployment, on which both readings agree (0001 §1, §6), so the program always has a-v. The run half, the status ids and the result, is N2's, which implements sleep.
cases.title: final sleep adds a-v
every nested body list gets its own virtual step

files.f/x/main.flow/flow.yaml:
value:
  modules:
    - id: l
      value:
        type: forloopflow
        iterator: {type: static, value: [1]}
        modules:
          - id: b
            sleep: {type: static, value: 1}
            value: {type: identity}
    - id: o
      value:
        type: branchone
        branches:
          - expr: 'true'
            modules:
              - id: c
                sleep: {type: static, value: 1}
                value: {type: identity}
        default:
          - id: d
            sleep: {type: static, value: 1}
            value: {type: identity}
    - id: z
      value:
        type: branchall
        branches:
          - modules:
              - id: e
                sleep: {type: static, value: 1}
                value: {type: identity}

cases.title: a sleep that is not last adds nothing

cases.note: Ids are not unique in Windmill (OF-2), so a virtual id can repeat one written in the folder. The run's sites are those of the final list, so the occurrence counts the virtual step (0011).
cases.title: the virtual step counts in its list's occurrences

cases.note: OF-17 appends the virtual step to module lists; the failure and preprocessor modules sit in their own slots.
cases.title: the failure module is a slot, not a list

note: The virtual `<id>-v` identity after a final sleep, at every level. A final suspend would add it too, but suspend is refused at load (FX-39).
